2026-08-18T12:31:14.2305216Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2305839Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2306386Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2307357Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2308765Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2309579Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2312039Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2315671Z >
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2320834Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2324870Z >
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2328257Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2342258Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2342627Z ### How to Use
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2343057Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2346134Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2347578Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2347889Z ```bash
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2348899Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2350610Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2351715Z ```
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2352076Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2353114Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2354818Z ```bash
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2357349Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2358740Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2371679Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2379169Z ```
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2411297Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2418471Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2420036Z ```bash
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2420984Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2445687Z ```
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2446951Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2447709Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2449343Z ```bash
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2450227Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2451645Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2452809Z ```
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2453150Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2453599Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2454288Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2456786Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2459389Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2459684Z ```bash
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2460446Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2461876Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2463213Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2463876Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2464700Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2466357Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2467898Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2468698Z ```
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2469049Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2470242Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2471704Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2471986Z ```bash
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2473089Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2474522Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2475694Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2476577Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2477254Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2478581Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2479485Z ```
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2479829Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2480218Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2481503Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2483069Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2484623Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2486220Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2488241Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2489104Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2489391Z ### Notes
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2489759Z 
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2490757Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2493032Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2495048Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2497277Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2499220Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2501549Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2507189Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-18T12:31:14.2508383Z </mcp-clis>
